einzeiler: Ana Navarro and Brian Teta wrap up season 29, discussing politics, Rosie O'Donnell and…
kurzfassung: Ana Navarro joins Brian Teta on the final episode of the season to discuss potential 2028 presidential contenders, including Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and J.B. Pritzker. They also cover recent political debates surrounding the Smithsonian, Daniel Ortega's grip on Nicaragua, and Rosie O'Donnell's one-woman show. The hosts close out the season by reflecting on their favorite guest interviews and celebrating the milestone of reaching fifty.
stichpunkte: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez leads early poll numbers for a potential 2028 Democratic presidential primary field.
J.B. Pritzker draws praise for his relatable background, self-deprecating humor, and perceived empathy.
Debates emerge around congressional scrutiny of the Smithsonian and the cultural meaning of Latina power.
Nicaraguan leadership comparisons highlight ongoing concerns over democratic backsliding and institutional strength.
Rosie O'Donnell receives praise for her vulnerable and poignant new one-woman theater show.
Season highlights include memorable visits from Richard J. Gere, J.D. Vance, and the cast of Christopher Nolan's latest film.
The hosts celebrate the conclusion of their award-winning 29th season and look ahead to upcoming episodes.

beschreibung:
Ana Navarro sits down with executive producer Brian Teta to react to Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez leading early 2028 presidential polls and explain why she believes JB Pritzker is the Democratic candidate to watch. Ana shares what she’s looking for in a future president, saying, “I want a president capable of empathy, humanity, and compassion.”

She also opens up about Nicaraguan President Daniel Ortega’s announcement that elections will no longer be held in the country and why the news is especially personal to her.

Plus, Ana dishes on attending her friend Rosie O’Donnell’s new one-woman show and joins Brian in celebrating the final episode of 'Behind the Table' and the end of Season 29 of 'The View'.
